subtopics.title: The TCP Connection
subtopics.summary: Why TCP is connection-oriented: the two processes must handshake before sending data, and each end maintains connection state (buffers, variables, sequence numbers). Covers point-to-point, full-duplex service and the maximum segment size (MSS).

subtopics.title: TCP Segment Structure
subtopics.summary: Anatomy of the TCP segment: source/destination port numbers, 32-bit sequence and acknowledgment numbers (byte-stream offsets), header flags (ACK, RST, SYN, FIN), receive window, checksum, options, and data payload.

subtopics.title: RTT Estimation and Timeout
subtopics.summary: How TCP measures SampleRTT and computes EstimatedRTT and DevRTT using exponential weighted moving averages, sets TimeoutInterval, and doubles the timeout after a retransmission timeout.

subtopics.title: TCP Reliable Data Transfer
subtopics.summary: How TCP provides reliability over an unreliable IP layer: cumulative acknowledgments, a single retransmission timer, sender events (ACK receipt, timeout, retransmission), and fast retransmit triggered by three duplicate ACKs.

subtopics.title: TCP Flow Control
subtopics.summary: The speed-matching service that prevents the sender from overflowing the receiver's buffer: the receive window (rwnd) advertised in segment headers and how the sender limits unacknowledged data to this window.

subtopics.title: TCP Connection Management
subtopics.summary: The connection lifecycle: the three-way handshake (SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK) with sequence number selection, connection teardown using FIN segments and ACKs, and the resulting client/server state transitions.
